items.definition: A name is the word people use to call a person, pet, or thing. You say your name when you meet someone.
items.example: My dog's name is Max.
items.picture_idea: A name tag reading 'Hello, my name is...' stuck on a shirt
items.definition_previous: The word that people call a person, animal, or thing.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a language unit by which a person or thing is known

items.definition: You say new when something was just made or bought. A new toy is not old or used yet.
items.example: I have new shoes today.
items.picture_idea: A shiny pair of shoes with a bow in a box
items.definition_previous: Just made or bought; not old.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: not of long duration; having just (or relatively recently) come into being or been made or acquired or discovered

items.definition: Night is when it is dark outside, after the sun goes down. Many people sleep at night.
items.example: The stars come out at night.
items.picture_idea: A dark sky with a moon and stars over a house
items.definition_previous: The time when it is dark and people usually sleep.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the time after sunset and before sunrise while it is dark outside

items.definition: Your nose is on your face, above your mouth. You use it to smell things and to breathe air.
items.example: The flower smells nice to my nose.
items.picture_idea: A smiling child's face with the nose highlighted
items.definition_previous: The part of your face that you use to smell and breathe.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the organ of smell and entrance to the respiratory tract; the prominent part of the face of man or other mammals

items.definition: A number tells you how many there are, like 1, 2, or 3. You use numbers when you count.
items.example: What number comes after five?
items.picture_idea: Colorful wooden blocks showing the numbers 1 2 3
items.definition_previous: A word or sign that tells how many, like 1, 2, or 3.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a concept of quantity involving zero and units

items.definition: You say off when something is not on any more. You can take shoes off or turn a light off.
items.explanation: Off is the opposite of on. It can describe a light, a TV, or something that comes away from a thing.
items.example: Please turn the light off.
items.picture_idea: A hand flipping a light switch down with the lamp dark
items.definition_previous: Not on; away from a place or not working.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: no longer on or in contact or attached

items.definition: You open a shut door or box so you can get in or look inside. Say open when you need something opened.
items.example: She opens the door for her brother.
items.picture_idea: A child pulling open a door or lifting a box lid
items.definition_previous: To move something so that things can go in or out, or so you can see inside.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: cause to open or to become open

items.definition: An orange is a round fruit with a thick skin. You peel it and eat the juicy pieces inside.
items.explanation: Orange is also a color, the color of this fruit.
items.example: I peeled an orange for my snack.
items.picture_idea: A round orange fruit with a few peeled segments
items.definition_previous: A round, juicy fruit with a thick orange skin.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: round yellow to orange fruit of any of several citrus trees

items.definition: You say over when something moves above another thing and across it. You can jump over a puddle.
items.example: The cow jumped over the moon.
items.picture_idea: A ball flying over a fence
items.definition_previous: Above something, or from one side of something to the other.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: Paper is thin, flat stuff that you write or draw on. Books, notes, and cards are made of it.
items.example: I drew a picture on the paper.
items.picture_idea: A stack of white paper with a crayon drawing on top
items.definition_previous: Thin, flat sheets that you write or draw on.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a material made of cellulose pulp derived mainly from wood or rags or certain grasses

items.definition: A park is an open place outside with grass and trees. People go there to play and walk.
items.example: We go to the park on Saturday.
items.picture_idea: A playground with swings, grass, and trees
items.definition_previous: An outdoor place with grass and trees where people play.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a piece of open land for recreational use in an urban area

items.definition: You pick when you choose one thing from a group. You can also pick a flower or an apple off a plant.
items.example: You can pick a red apple from the tree.
items.picture_idea: A child reaching up to pick an apple from a tree
items.definition_previous: To choose something, or to take something off a plant with your hand.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: select carefully from a group

items.definition_batch: You pick a flower or fruit when you take it off the plant with your hand.

edited.why: the choose meaning was lost; it matters most on a board

items.definition: You play when you have fun with toys or games. Say play when you want to join in a game.
items.example: The children play in the yard.
items.picture_idea: Two children kicking a ball in a yard
items.definition_previous: To have fun with games or toys.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be at play; be engaged in playful activity; amuse oneself in a way characteristic of children

items.definition: You say please when you ask for something, to be kind and polite. Say it before or after you ask.
items.example: Can I have some water, please?
items.picture_idea: A child with hands together asking politely
items.definition_previous: A polite word you say when you ask for something.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You pull when you hold something and make it move toward you. You pull a rope, a door, or a wagon.
items.example: He will pull the wagon up the hill.
items.picture_idea: A child pulling a red wagon by its handle
items.definition_previous: To hold something and move it toward you.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: cause to move by pulling

items.definition: You put a thing in a place when you set it there. Say put to tell where something should go.
items.example: Please put your coat on the hook.
items.picture_idea: A child placing a coat on a hook
items.definition_previous: To move something to a place and leave it there.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: put into a certain place or abstract location

items.definition: A queen is a woman who is the ruler of a country. She often wears a crown.
items.example: The queen wore a gold crown.
items.picture_idea: A woman in a long gown wearing a gold crown on a throne
items.definition_previous: A woman who rules a country, or the wife of a king.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a female sovereign ruler

items.definition: Quick means fast, or taking only a short time. A quick snack is ready in a few minutes.
items.example: The rabbit is quick.
items.picture_idea: A rabbit running fast with motion lines behind it
items.definition_previous: Fast; taking only a short time.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: accomplished rapidly and without delay

items.definition: Quiet means making little or no sound. A library is quiet, so people talk softly there.
items.example: Be quiet because the baby is sleeping.
items.picture_idea: A child holding a finger to their lips beside a sleeping baby
items.definition_previous: Making little or no sound.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: free of noise or uproar; or making little if any sound

items.definition: A rabbit is a small animal with soft fur, long ears, and a short fluffy tail. It hops.
items.example: The rabbit ate a carrot.
items.picture_idea: A fluffy rabbit with long ears eating a carrot
items.definition_previous: A small furry animal with long ears that hops.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: any of various burrowing animals of the family Leporidae having long ears and short tails; some domesticated and raised for pets or food

items.definition: Rain is water that falls from clouds in small drops. You get wet if you stand outside in it.
items.example: I wear boots when there is rain.
items.picture_idea: Gray clouds with raindrops falling on a puddle and an umbrella
items.definition_previous: Water that falls from the clouds in drops.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: water falling in drops from vapor condensed in the atmosphere

items.definition: You read when you look at words and know what they say. You read books, signs, and messages.
items.explanation: The past form is spelled the same as read but sounds like 'red'.
items.example: I read a book before bed.
items.picture_idea: A child sitting with an open picture book
items.definition_previous: To look at words and understand them.
items.example_previous: My mom reads a story to me every night.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: interpret something that is written or printed

items.definition: Red is the color of a ripe tomato or a fire truck. Stop signs are red too.
items.example: She has a red balloon.
items.picture_idea: A bright red balloon
items.definition_previous: The color of a ripe tomato or a fire truck.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: of a color at the end of the color spectrum (next to orange); resembling the color of blood or cherries or tomatoes or rubies

items.definition: A road is a long, hard path for cars and buses to drive on.
items.example: Look both ways before you cross the road.
items.picture_idea: A paved road with a car and a crosswalk
items.definition_previous: A long hard path where cars and buses drive.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: an open way (generally public) for travel or transportation

items.definition: You run when you move fast on your feet, faster than a walk. You run to catch a ball.
items.example: The dog can run very fast.
items.picture_idea: A child running across a field
items.definition_previous: To move on your feet very fast.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move fast by using one's feet, with one foot off the ground at any given time

items.definition: You feel sad when something makes you want to cry. You say "I am sad" to tell people how you feel.
items.example: I felt sad when my friend moved away.
items.picture_idea: A child with a frown and a tear on the cheek
items.definition_previous: Feeling unhappy.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: experiencing or showing sorrow or unhappiness

items.definition: A school is a place where you go to learn from teachers. Many children go there on most weekdays.
items.example: I walk to school with my sister.
items.picture_idea: A school building with a bell and children arriving
items.definition_previous: A place where children go to learn.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a building where young people receive education

items.definition: You use see to say what your eyes show you. If you look and a bird is there, you see it.
items.example: I can see a bird in the tree.
items.picture_idea: A child looking up at a bird in a tree
items.definition_previous: To use your eyes to know what is there.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: perceive by sight or have the power to perceive by sight

items.definition: You sit when your bottom rests on a chair or the floor. You sit down to rest, eat, or listen.
items.example: Please sit down on the chair.
items.picture_idea: A child sitting on a chair at a table
items.definition_previous: To rest with your bottom on a chair or the floor.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be in a position in which one's upper body is largely upright and supported by one's backside

items.definition: When you sleep, your eyes are closed and your body rests. You sleep at night in your bed.
items.example: The baby sleeps in a small bed.
items.picture_idea: A child asleep in bed under a blanket with 'Zzz' above
items.definition_previous: To rest with your eyes closed and your mind quiet.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be asleep

items.definition: Snow is soft white stuff that falls from the sky when it is very cold. You can make a snowman with it.
items.example: We made a snowman in the snow.
items.picture_idea: Snowflakes falling on a snowman in a yard
items.definition_previous: Soft white flakes of frozen water that fall from the sky when it is cold.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: precipitation falling from clouds in the form of ice crystals

items.definition: Soft means nice to touch and not hard. A pillow is soft, and so is a kitten's fur.
items.example: The kitten has soft fur.
items.picture_idea: A hand petting a fluffy kitten
items.definition_previous: Nice and gentle to touch; not hard.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: yielding readily to pressure or weight

items.definition: A table has a flat top and legs. You put food, books, or other things on it.
items.example: We eat dinner at the table.
items.picture_idea: A wooden table with plates and cups on it
items.definition_previous: A piece of furniture with a flat top and legs.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a piece of furniture having a smooth flat top that is usually supported by one or more vertical legs

items.definition: You take something when you pick it up and have it with you. You take your bag when you go out.
items.example: Take your lunch box to school.
items.picture_idea: A child picking up a lunch box from a table
items.definition_previous: To get something and carry it with you, or to pick it up.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: take something or somebody with oneself somewhere

items.definition: Tall means big from the bottom to the top. A giraffe is tall, and so is a tree.
items.example: The giraffe is very tall.
items.picture_idea: A giraffe standing next to a small tree
items.definition_previous: Having a lot of height; high from bottom to top.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: great in vertical dimension; high in stature

items.definition: You tell someone something when you say it so they know it. You tell a friend your name.
items.example: Tell me your name.
items.picture_idea: One child whispering to another child
items.definition_previous: To say something to someone so they know it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: express in words

items.definition: A tree is a very tall plant with a thick trunk, branches, and leaves. Birds can build nests in a tree.
items.example: A bird built a nest in the tree.
items.picture_idea: A large tree with green leaves and a bird nest
items.definition_previous: A tall plant with a thick trunk, branches, and leaves.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a tall perennial woody plant having a main trunk and branches forming a distinct elevated crown; includes both gymnosperms and angiosperms

items.definition: You turn when you move to face a new way. You turn left to go down a different street.
items.explanation: It can also mean your chance to do something in a game, as in 'It is my turn.'
items.example: Turn left at the corner.
items.picture_idea: A bike at a corner with an arrow pointing left
items.definition_previous: To move around or change direction.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: to change orientation or direction

items.definition: You say under when one thing is lower down and another thing is over it. A ball can roll under a bed.
items.example: The cat is under the table.
items.picture_idea: A cat sitting beneath a table
items.definition_previous: Below something; in a lower place than something.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You use something when you pick it to do a job. You use a spoon to eat soup.
items.example: I use a spoon to eat soup.
items.picture_idea: A child eating soup with a spoon
items.definition_previous: To do a job with something.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: put into service; make work or employ for a particular purpose or for its inherent or natural purpose

items.definition: You say very to make a word stronger. A very hot soup is hotter than a hot soup.
items.explanation: We put very before an adjective or adverb to make it stronger.
items.example: The soup is very hot.
items.definition_previous: A lot; more than usual.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: used to give emphasis

items.definition: You walk when you move by stepping with one foot and then the other. You walk to the shop.
items.example: We walk to the store together.
items.picture_idea: Two people walking along a sidewalk
items.definition_previous: To move by putting one foot in front of the other.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: use one's feet to advance; advance by steps

items.definition: You say want when you would like to have or do something. You say "I want water" when you are thirsty.
items.example: I want a drink of milk.
items.picture_idea: A child pointing at a glass of milk
items.definition_previous: To wish for something or need to have it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: feel or have a desire for; want strongly

items.definition: Water is the clear liquid you drink. Rain, rivers, and the sea are made of water.
items.example: I drink a glass of water.
items.picture_idea: A clear glass being filled from a tap
items.definition_previous: The clear liquid that we drink and that fills rivers and seas.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: binary compound that occurs at room temperature as a clear colorless odorless tasteless liquid; freezes into ice below 0 degrees centigrade and boils above 100 degrees centigrade; widely used as a solvent

items.definition: You say wet when something has water on it and is not dry. Your socks get wet if you step in a puddle.
items.example: My socks are wet from the puddle.
items.picture_idea: A child standing in a puddle with soaked socks
items.definition_previous: Covered with water or another liquid; not dry.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: covered or soaked with a liquid such as water

items.definition: A window is a piece of glass in a wall. You look through it, and light comes in.
items.example: I look out of the window at the rain.
items.picture_idea: A window with raindrops on the glass and a view of a garden
items.definition_previous: A hole in a wall with glass in it that lets in light.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a framework of wood or metal that contains a glass windowpane and is built into a wall or roof to admit light or air

items.definition: Yellow is the color of a banana or the sun. The middle of an egg is yellow too.
items.example: The duck has a yellow beak.
items.picture_idea: A bright yellow rubber duck
items.definition_previous: The color of a banana or the sun.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: of the color intermediate between green and orange in the color spectrum; of something resembling the color of an egg yolk

items.definition: A zoo is a place where you can go to see wild animals. The animals live there and people visit them.
items.example: We saw a lion at the zoo.
items.picture_idea: A zoo entrance with a lion and an elephant behind a fence
items.definition_previous: A place where people can see wild animals that live in cages or large areas.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the facility where wild animals are housed for exhibition
